description: Phasing effect built from pitch-shift packets: splits a MONO source into 'streams' parallel copies whose phase shifts forward then back within packets at 'phasfrq' Hz, up to 'shift' semitones of maximum phase-shift per packet, and mixes them to 'ochans' output channels - the classic swept-comb 'jet' phasing as a time-domain packet process. Duration: indur + offset/1000 - static plus the stream time-offset (2.0005 from a 2 s source at offset 0, +1 packet-grid window; exactly +0.2 s at -o200, verified). BREAKPOINTS: phasfrq and shift both capable (each verified distinct from both scalar endpoints; a phasfrq brk also perturbs length by the packet grid - 2.0071); the banner warns extreme phasfrq changes/reversals 'will produce anomalous output'. Ranges verbatim: streams '(2.000000 to 8.000000)'; shift '(0.000000 to 12.000000)'; offset '(0.000000 to 500.000000)' ms; ochans must not exceed streams ('ERROR: INVALID DATA / ERROR: Number of output channels exceeds number of streams.'). ochans 1 and 2 both verified (mono or stereo phasing; ochans > 2 is loudspeaker-array territory - the -s surround flag only applies there). Deterministic (pairs 1.3 s apart byte-identical; no randomness, no seed). MONO input only ('File st2.wav is not of correct type (must be mono)').
musical_use: The swept-jet phaser as an offline gesture: streams 3-6 with shift 2-6 st at phasfrq 0.5-4 Hz gives the breathing, hollow comb-sweep on anything sustained - pads, cymbals, noise beds, vocal drones. phasfrq is the sweep rate (breakpoint it to accelerate the swirl or freeze it mid-sweep); shift is intensity (0 = dry-ish stack, 12 = seasick); more streams = denser, smoother swirl. ochans 2 gives instant stereo motion from a mono source - the streams distribute across the pair (set ochans 1 to keep it mono-compatible). offset (up to 500 ms) staggers the streams for thicker, chorus-like blur at the cost of a longer file. Feed it broadband material - phasing needs spectrum to comb. For resonant sweeps use filter sweeping; for spectral undulation try blur/focus family.

streams.description: Number of phase-interacting streams (CDP-enforced 2-8, 9 refused verbatim). More streams = denser swirl.

phasfrq.description: Packet frequency - the phase sweeps forward then back once per packet, so this is the audible sweep rate. Breakpoint-capable (verified: 1->8 ramp distinct from both scalar endpoints); banner warns extreme changes or reversals produce anomalous output. A brk also nudges total length via the packet grid (+0.35% observed).

shift.description: Maximum phase-shift within a packet, 0-12 semitones (CDP-enforced, 13 refused verbatim). Intensity dial: 0 near-dry, 12 extreme warble. Breakpoint-capable (verified distinct from both endpoints).

ochans.description: Output channel count; must not exceed streams ('Number of output channels exceeds number of streams.', INVALID DATA verbatim). 1 = mono mix, 2 = stereo distribution (both verified); > 2 builds loudspeaker arrays - DAW/spatial territory, keep at 1-2 in the engine.

offset.description: Time-offset of the most-offset stream (others staggered between 0 and it), 0-500 ms (CDP-enforced, 600 refused verbatim). Adds itself to the output length exactly (+0.2 s at 200 ms, verified).

examples.description: Slow stereo jet-swirl on a sustained bed.
examples.expected_use: Classic phaser sweep once per second, distributed across the stereo pair; output = indur + one packet window.
sweep.brk '0 0.5 / 8 6' speeds the sweep up across 8 s; the 150 ms stagger thickens it (output +0.15 s).

known_issues: Duration = indur + offset/1000 (+ up to one packet window: +0.02% at offset 0); a phasfrq breakpoint perturbs length slightly via the packet grid.

MONO input only (verbatim refusal); ochans <= streams (INVALID DATA verbatim). ochans > 2 assumes a loudspeaker array (banner; -s surround switch applies only there) - out of the engine's stereo scope, use execute() if ever needed.

phasfrq/shift breakpoints verified capable; streams/ochans/offset are scalar (structural). Banner warns extreme phasfrq motion 'will produce anomalous output' - keep ramps smooth; -e prints rounding-error warnings for time-shifted streams.
